rv.q: And the actor makes that seem perfectly natural in a gripping, no-holds-barred performance that will impress fans of his work in the X-Men movies and unlock for youthful newcomers to Shakespeare some of the poetic and psychological riches of the play.
This is a gripping and genuinely startling production - and would be more effective still with a speedier running time.
Be ready, too, for an excellent and harrowing performance from McAvoy.

Jamie Lloyd's production is equally thrilling and radical, and is set 50 years hence in a (possibly) post-independence Scotland, brutalised by war and, we may assume from the programme notes, ravaged by the effects of climate change.
This production is a breath of fresh air, a play from the past that is most definitely for the present.
This is sinewy, grimy Shakespeare that finds full expression for the play’s extraordinarily terrifying imagery – and is a terrific start to Lloyd’s new season at the Trafalgar.

cn.t: Critics largely praise Jamie Lloyd's visceral, dystopian staging and McAvoy's raw, commanding performance, making this modern reimagining of Macbeth a gripping, politically resonant success.
